_metadata.description: Golden eval set for the SLO Review Board Agent. Each case is a known-input → known-correct-verdict pair. Cases are compact on purpose (real docs are longer); the verdict-determining signal must be present, not every operational detail. All services are fictional.

cases.description: Well-designed portfolio for a checkout service. Should pass all four tests.
cases.discovery: Service: checkout-service. Owner: Payments Platform team. Consumers: ~50M monthly active users via web and mobile apps. User journey: user clicks checkout, fills payment, receives confirmation. Hard dependencies: Stripe API (99.99% per Stripe SLA), internal user-service (99.95% measured). Incident history: 3 outages in last 12 months — 2 caused by Stripe degradation, 1 by user-service auth bug. Business has a public SLA: 99.9% checkout availability. Observability: Datadog metrics + traces.
cases.implementation_guide:
Three proposed SLOs:
1. Checkout success rate — SLI: HTTP 2xx on POST /checkout / total POST /checkout. Target: 99.9% over 28 days. Basis: matches public SLA.
2. Checkout latency — SLI: P95 latency on POST /checkout. Target: 95% of requests < 3s over 28 days. Basis: observed P95 over last 90 days has been 2.4s; 3s gives 25% headroom.
3. Payment confirmation latency — SLI: P95 time from checkout submit to confirmation email sent. Target: 95% < 60s over 28 days. Basis: customer NPS drops measurably when confirmations exceed 60s (data from CX team Q3 survey).
All three use Datadog as the tool of record. Budgeting: Occurrences method.

cases.description: Solid portfolio but one SLO is cause-based and should be demoted. Target on another lacks basis.
cases.discovery: Service: notification-service. Owner: Platform team. Consumers: 200 internal microservices that publish notifications to be delivered via email, SMS, push. Hard dependencies: SendGrid (99.95% SLA), Twilio (99.95% SLA), Firebase Cloud Messaging (no published SLO). Incidents: 5 in past year — 3 from SendGrid throttling, 2 from internal Redis queue saturation.
cases.implementation_guide:
Four proposed SLOs:
1. Email delivery success — SLI: SendGrid delivered/total emails. Target: 99.5% over 28 days. Basis: matches SendGrid SLA floor.
2. SMS delivery success — SLI: Twilio delivered/total SMS. Target: 99.5% over 28 days. Basis: matches Twilio SLA floor.
3. Push delivery success — SLI: FCM ack rate. Target: 99.9% over 28 days. Basis: 99.9% is industry standard for push.
4. Redis queue health — SLI: Redis memory usage < 80%. Target: 99% of samples over 28 days. Basis: prevents the 2 outages we had last year.

cases.description: Five out of seven SLOs are cause-based. Structural failure — requires rescope, not revision.
cases.discovery: Service: order-fulfillment-service. Consumers: warehouse staff at 12 distribution centers. Critical user journey: scan barcode, system tells worker which bin, worker picks item, system confirms. Hard dependencies: WMS-DB (PostgreSQL, no documented SLO), internal auth (99.9%), barcode scanner gateway. Incident history: heavy — 14 incidents in past 6 months, mostly during peak shifts.
cases.implementation_guide:
Seven proposed SLOs:
1. CPU utilization < 75% — Target: 99% of samples. Basis: stops overload incidents.
2. Memory utilization < 80% — Target: 99% of samples. Basis: prevents OOM.
3. Disk utilization < 90% — Target: 99% of samples. Basis: storage discipline.
4. Database connection pool < 90% — Target: 99% of samples. Basis: stops connection exhaustion.
5. Service process running — Target: 99.9%. Basis: prevents downtime.
6. Barcode scan success — SLI: scans returning a bin assignment / total scans. Target: 99.9% over 28 days. Basis: '99.9% is the standard.'
7. End-to-end pick latency — SLI: P95 time from scan to bin assignment. Target: 95% < 2s. Basis: workers have stated 2s is the workflow threshold.

cases.description: Executive summary commits to 3 SLOs; body defines 8. One SLO is duplicated with different targets. Structural disqualification.
cases.discovery: Service: user-profile-service. Consumers: mobile app, web app, partner APIs. Hard dependencies: identity-provider (99.95%), profile-db (99.9%). Recent incidents: 4 in 12 months, 3 from identity-provider.
cases.implementation_guide:
Executive summary: 'We propose three SLOs covering availability, latency, and data freshness.'

Body:
1. API availability — SLI: HTTP 2xx/total. Target: 99.9%.
2. API latency — SLI: P95 < 500ms. Target: 95% under 500ms.
3. Data freshness — SLI: max age of cache entry. Target: < 60s.
4. Authentication success rate — SLI: identity-provider verifications passing/total. Target: 99.95%.
5. Profile read latency — SLI: P95 read latency. Target: 95% < 200ms.
6. Profile write latency — SLI: P95 write latency. Target: 95% < 500ms.
7. Cache hit rate — SLI: cache hits/total reads. Target: 90%.
8. API availability — SLI: HTTP 2xx/total. Target: 99.99%.

cases.description: Availability portfolio is solid but no latency SLO despite discovery flagging latency complaints.
cases.discovery: Service: search-service. Consumers: e-commerce shoppers, ~20M MAU. Key user journey: user types query, sees results. Pain point named in discovery: 'shoppers complain results take too long during peak traffic — Black Friday produced 6-second average response, NPS dropped 15 points that week.' Hard dependencies: Elasticsearch cluster (no documented SLO, internal team).
cases.implementation_guide:
Two proposed SLOs:
1. Search API availability — SLI: 2xx/total on GET /search. Target: 99.95% over 28 days. Basis: 12-month observed availability is 99.97%.
2. Search result freshness — SLI: max age of index update. Target: < 5 min over 28 days. Basis: business requirement for new-listing visibility.

cases.description: Single SLO portfolio. Target is plausible but the document offers no basis for it.
cases.discovery: Service: webhook-delivery. Consumers: 300 enterprise customers integrating outbound webhooks. Hard dependencies: customer-controlled endpoints (no SLO), internal retry queue. No stated business SLA. Incident history: 'occasional customer complaints about webhook lag, no formal SLA agreement in place.'
cases.implementation_guide:
One proposed SLO:
1. Webhook delivery success — SLI: webhooks delivered within 60s / total webhooks. Target: 99.5% over 28 days. Basis: 'industry standard for webhook delivery.'
